item.title: Republican 'cavalry' arrives with a Trump-backed $150 million ad blitz in key races
item.description: To counter a difficult political environment, two Trump-aligned super PACs have reserved more than $150 million in ads — primarily in deep red House and Senate races that have now become competitive.

item.title: A DHS email raises new questions about the Trump administration's election plans
item.description: A heavily redacted email from last year, reported first by NPR, reveals that DHS personnel shared a list of jurisdictions that offer election materials in non-English languages. It's unclear why.

item.title: Could trees developed with gene-editing technology protect Florida's citrus industry?
item.description: A bacterial infection is wiping out Florida's citrus trees. Growers hope a rootstock developed with gene-editing technology could keep the disease at bay.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: What to know after a week of Houthi attacks that threaten Saudi oil
item.description: The Houthis' biggest land grab in years reignited Yemen's 12-year civil war and pushed up global fuel prices, extending their reach to a key maritime chokepoint and threatening Saudi Arabia's oil exports.

item.description: The latest lawsuit, first reported by NPR, argues the Trump administration's repeated suggestions that federal officers could be at polling sites is a form of illegal voter intimidation.

item.title: The driver who slammed into an LA bus before helicopter crash is charged with murder
item.description: An SUV driver was under the influence of drugs when she swerved into the wrong lane, blew a red light and slammed into a Los Angeles city bus, killing two riders, prosecutors said as they charged her with murder.
